BiblicalUsage: Tel-abib was a settlement of the exiles by the river Chebar in Babylonia. Ezekiel came to them of the captivity at Tel-abib, that dwelt by the river of Chebar, and sat where they sat, and remained there astonished among them seven days.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Tel-abib is the exile's address, and the prophet sat seven days in silence before he spoke a word.
